subject: 5G Small Cell Wireless Infrastructure Policy
overview: The Council approved extensive amendments to the city’s interim 5G small cell policy following a lengthy debate over health concerns and deployment proximity to residences. Additionally, the Fire Chief provided an operational update on equipment procurement, and residents contested the school committee’s process for renaming city buildings.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognition
items.summary: Approved a resolution congratulating Terry Cotter on being named Medford’s first Poet Laureate.

items.title: Fire Department Operational Update
items.summary: Fire Chief Giliberti reported that two new ladder trucks are expected in June and provided updates on fire station roof and kitchen repairs and pending new hires.

items.title: Fire Mutual Aid Reauthorization
items.summary: Approved the reauthorization of the Metro Fire Mutual Aid Agreement through October 2021.

items.title: Winthrop Street Construction Concerns
items.summary: Tabled a resolution requesting that Eversource and the City Engineer explain road cutouts and debris storage on Winthrop Street.

items.title: 5G Small Cell Interim Policy Review
items.summary: Approved a resolution and eight amendments to the city’s interim 5G policy, requesting a federal moratorium on deployment and establishing stricter setback requirements from residential dwellings.

items.title: International Transgender Day of Visibility
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating the transgender and non-binary community and noting support for equal rights.

items.title: PILOT and Institutional Master Plan Legislation
items.summary: Referred support for state bills regarding mandatory PILOT payments and institutional master plans to the Subcommittee on Intergovernmental Affairs.

items.title: Billboard Impact Fee Expenditures
items.summary: Requested an itemized list of expenditures from the $250,000 Clear Channel billboard impact fee received in fiscal year 2021.

items.title: Fells Avenue Traffic Safety
items.summary: Referred a request for speed trailers and additional safety improvements at Fells Avenue and Hickory Avenue to the Committee of the Whole.

items.title: KP Law Invoices and Spending
items.summary: Requested a detailed accounting of legal fees and invoices paid to KP Law outside of their monthly retainer.

items.title: Public Participation: Naming of Public Property
items.summary: Residents and former officials debated the school committee’s decision to rename the Columbus School and urged the Council to establish formal ordinances for naming city property.

items.title: Condolences and Minutes
items.summary: Approved routine condolences for Allan McDougal, Irma Cassisio, and Joseph DeRocco and accepted the meeting minutes from March 2021.
